title: Anomaly detection in IR images of PV modules using supervised contrastive learning
mechanism: Supervised contrastive training of a ResNet-34 plus kNN distance as anomaly score, evaluated as train-on-one-plant, test-on-another (unsupervised domain adaptation framing).
evidence: R: AUROC 73.3 to 96.6 % on 9 source-target combinations of 4 plants, 2.92 M IR module images, 8.5 % anomalous; at a fixed threshold 79.4 % normal and 77.1 % anomalous correct; sometimes beats a BCE classifier; insensitive to hyperparameters.
adaptation: Add a SupCon auxiliary loss on cell-pooled layer4 features (positives = same cell label crack / inactive / clean, sampled across the 5 sources) to the PF fine-tune, aimed at the E1 gap; adopt the source-to-target protocol as the model for the benchmark's unseen-module split.
min_experiment: Arm PF + SupCon aux (weight 0.1), 3 seeds; baseline PF, 3 seeds; metrics E1 crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU, test clean-49 crack IoU; kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.02 or test crack IoU drops > 0.01.
prior_overlap: none. BRIEF 5 tested MIM / DDeP pool pretraining and Mean Teacher, not a supervised contrastive auxiliary loss during fine-tuning.
